dossier.purpose: gVisor is an application kernel written in Go that implements a Linux-like syscall interface in userspace (the 'Sentry'), with a separate file-proxy process (the 'Gofer') and its own TCP/IP stack (netstack). It ships as the OCI runtime `runsc` plus a containerd shim, so Docker/Kubernetes/containerd workloads, or single commands via `runsc do`, the bubblewrap-style `runsc bwrap` CLI, `runsc sandboxexec`, or the experimental Go/Python 'SandboxExec' SDKs, run against the Sentry instead of directly against the host kernel. Filesystem and network restriction is configured by the operator (OCI mounts/overlay and `--network=sandbox|host|none`); the project's own README says it is not a tool to 'limit the scope of access for a service'. Linux hosts only (x86_64/ARM64).

claims.claim: gVisor provides a strong layer of isolation between running applications and the host OS; it is an application kernel implementing a Linux-like interface, written in a memory-safe language (Go) and running in userspace.
Includes an OCI runtime called `runsc` that integrates with Docker and Kubernetes.
Not a syscall filter (e.g. seccomp-bpf) nor a wrapper over Linux isolation primitives (e.g. firejail, AppArmor), and not a VM; 'a distinct third approach'.
Containers are not a sandbox: with a shared kernel, 'container escape is possible with a single vulnerability'.
gVisor limits the host kernel surface accessible to the application and 'implements Linux by way of Linux'.

Should not be confused with tools to harden containers against external threats, provide integrity checks, or 'limit the scope of access for a service'; 'One should always be careful about what data is made available to a container.'
gVisor builds on x86_64 and ARM64.
Requirements (source build): Linux 5.6+ and Docker 17.09.0 or greater.

`make release-tarball DESTINATION=bin/` builds a tarball with `runsc`, `containerd-shim-runsc-v1` and sidecar binaries that `runsc` expects in a `gvisor-bin/` directory next to itself; extract to /usr/local/bin.
Direct Bazel use (no Docker wrapper) is possible but 'isn't recommended due to the extra overhead'.
macOS: 'Some packages support running tests directly on macOS' (needs bazel 8); no macOS runtime is described.
A synthetic `go` branch exists for importing gVisor Go packages (e.g. netstack); 'runsc builds from this branch are not supported'.

User docs live at gvisor.dev; security policy is SECURITY.md; governance is GOVERNANCE.md. The README itself contains no license statement (searched README.md for license/Apache/BSD/MIT: 0 matches); licensing is in the root LICENSE file.

install.command:
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y apt-transport-https ca-certificates curl gnupg
curl -fsSL https://gvisor.dev/archive.key | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/gvisor-archive-keyring.gpg
echo "deb [arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/gvisor-archive-keyring.gpg] https://storage.googleapis.com/gvisor/releases release main" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/gvisor.list > /dev/null
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y runsc

install.method: Latest release tarball with sha512 check (also needs gvisor-bin/ kept next to runsc)
install.command:
(
  set -e
  ARCH=$(uname -m)
  URL=https://storage.googleapis.com/gvisor/releases/release/latest/${ARCH}
  wget ${URL}/gvisor.tar.zstd ${URL}/gvisor.tar.zstd.sha512
  sha512sum -c gvisor.tar.zstd.sha512
  sudo tar --zstd -xf gvisor.tar.zstd -C /usr/local/bin
  rm -f gvisor.tar.zstd gvisor.tar.zstd.sha512
)

install.method: Register as a Docker runtime (edits Docker daemon config)
install.command:
sudo /usr/local/bin/runsc install
sudo systemctl reload docker
docker run --rm --runtime=runsc hello-world

make release-tarball DESTINATION=bin/
sudo tar -C /usr/local/bin -xf bin/gvisor.tar.bz2

install.method: Python SDK (experimental; runsc must be installed separately and found via RUNSC_PATH or PATH)
Go SDK (experimental) via the synthetic `go` branch (doc says to replace the path 'when available')

platforms.linux_x86_64: yes - README.md:60 ('builds on x86_64 and ARM64'); g3doc/user_guide/install.md:5; g3doc/user_guide/FAQ.md:9-12; CI runs AMD64 and ARM64 smoke, unit and syscall tests (.buildkite/pipeline.yaml:73-86,358-372,397-412). Default platform is systrap, no virtualization needed (runsc/config/flags.go:102; g3doc/architecture_guide/intro_to_gvisor.md:158-163). Sandbox-network mode needs root (intro_to_gvisor.md:219-226); a rootless path exists with limits (g3doc/user_guide/rootless.md:46-53).
platforms.wsl2: unknown - no mention of WSL, WSL2 or Windows Subsystem for Linux anywhere in the tree (searched all file types for WSL|WSL2|WSL1|Windows Subsystem for Linux|microsoft-standard: 0 matches) and no WSL2 CI job (.buildkite/pipeline.yaml). Upstream says only 'requires Linux 5.6+' (g3doc/user_guide/install.md:5) and 'Today, gVisor requires Linux' (g3doc/user_guide/FAQ.md:5-7). Whether a WSL2 kernel meets the seccomp/user-namespace/cgroup prerequisites is not documented (runsc/hostsettings/hostsettings.go:254-312 lists the user-namespace sysctls checked).
platforms.macos_arm64: no - g3doc/user_guide/FAQ.md:5-7 ('Today, gVisor requires Linux'); the project blog says 'gVisor works strictly on Linux systems' and that macOS/Windows use needs a Linux VM such as Docker Desktop (website/blog/2024-09-23-dangerzone.md:83-85,305-314); README.md:125-135 documents macOS only for running some Bazel test targets; CI only cross-builds selected netstack packages for darwin/arm64 (.buildkite/pipeline.yaml:146-156); the Python SDK classifies itself as POSIX :: Linux (sandboxexec/sandbox/python/pyproject.toml:16). No macOS install method is documented.
platforms.gpu: yes (Linux hosts) - NVIDIA GPUs via the in-sandbox `nvproxy` driver proxy on preselected open-driver versions (g3doc/user_guide/gpu.md:11-17; runsc/config/flags.go:184-190), plus TPU devices (g3doc/user_guide/compatibility.md:61-64); GPU CI jobs at .buildkite/pipeline.yaml:198-260.

integrations.cli: yes - `runsc` binary (runsc/main.go:18-32; subcommands registered in runsc/cli/maincli/maincli.go:49-103): OCI commands (create/run/exec/kill/delete...), `runsc do` (one-off command; 'to be used for testing only', runsc/cmd/do.go:67-81), `runsc bwrap` bubblewrap-style personality (also selected when the binary is invoked as `bwrap`: runsc/cmd/alias/aliases.go:35-44; g3doc/user_guide/personalities/bwrap.md:5-25; implemented inside runsc via an OCI bundle, runsc/cmd/alias/bwrap/bwrap.go:315-354; its parser recognises 26 flags and anything else fails with 'Unknown option': runsc/cmd/alias/bwrap/cli.go:182-227), `runsc sandboxexec` (runs a command per a SandboxOptions proto from --options or stdin: runsc/cmd/sandboxexec.go:39-111), `runsc install` (Docker runtime registration: runsc/cmd/install.go:53-55), plus metric/debug helpers (maincli.go:78-97).
integrations.mcp: none found - there is no MCP server for gVisor/runsc. The only MCP code in the tree is images/systemd-user/gnome-mcp/desktop_mcp.py, an MCP server that exposes a GNOME desktop as a computer-use tool and is run inside gVisor as a demo/test image (desktop_mcp.py:16,71-80); it is not a sandbox-control interface.
integrations.sdk_or_api: Go package gvisor.dev/gvisor/sandboxexec/sandbox (New/Exec/Close/Snapshot: sandboxexec/sandbox/sandbox.go:15-17,469,687,748) and Python package `gvisor` (Sandbox/Mount/MountType/NetworkMode/Error: sandboxexec/sandbox/python/gvisor/__init__.py:17-21; pyproject.toml:6-8). Both generate an OCI bundle and drive `runsc` as a subprocess located via RUNSC_PATH or PATH (sandbox.go:341-356,587-611,701-712; sandbox.py:382-423,444-450). Both are labelled experimental/'not meant for production use' (sandboxexec/README.md:3-4; g3doc/user_guide/sdk/go.md:3-4; python.md:3-4). Go SDK docs do not match the code (see claim_checks). Other interfaces: OCI runtime spec via runsc, containerd shim v2 (shim/main.go:15), Prometheus-style HTTP metrics via the opt-in `runsc metric-server` (g3doc/user_guide/observability.md:13-17), a mutating Kubernetes webhook (webhook/main.go:15). No documented HTTP/RPC control API for end users was found in g3doc.
integrations.claude_code_or_codex: none found - no documented Claude Code or Codex integration, plugin, hook or settings. Searches for claude|codex|MCP found only (a) contributor-workflow files for developing gVisor itself: .claude/skills/add-syscall/SKILL.md:1-24, .agents/skills/update-gvisor-maintainers/SKILL.md:1-11, AGENTS.md:1-47; and (b) project-blog material showing other agent harnesses (OpenClaw, PicoClaw, Hermes Agent) run under Docker `--runtime=runsc` (website/blog/2026-04-15-magi-multi-agent-gvisor-isolation.md:8-27), which itself says integrating gVisor into existing applications that need sandboxing is a current drawback 'being worked on' (same file:1318-1321).

readme.telemetry_and_network: No telemetry or phone-home code found in the runtime: keyword searches (telemetry, analytics, usage report, phone home) over Go/doc/script sources hit only the website's analytics ID (website/_config.yml:28) and an indirect `golang.org/x/telemetry` module in go.mod:117 that no gVisor Go file imports (repo-wide import search). `runsc` itself does not link net/http (runsc/cmd/install_sidecars.go:57-58). Metrics are opt-in and local: `--metric-server` defaults to empty (runsc/config/flags.go:89; g3doc/user_guide/observability.md:89-92) and the separate `runsc metric-server` sidecar serves Prometheus HTTP on a user-chosen address/UDS (observability.md:13-17,67-70). Network use: apt/tarball install fetches from gvisor.dev and storage.googleapis.com (g3doc/user_guide/install.md:27-28,51-53); `runsc install` can auto-download missing sidecars from storage.googleapis.com via curl/wget (runsc/cmd/install.go:69-73; runsc/cmd/install_sidecars.go:46-70; install.md:84-101; slated for removal end of Sept 2026 but still present at this tag) and rewrites Docker daemon config (install.go:53-55,64). An optional GCS checkpoint gofer (runsc/checkpointgofer/main.go:37-53; runsc/sandbox/sandbox.go:609-630,1799-1811) uses Google Cloud credentials only when a checkpoint image path resolves to a GCS URI. No account or hosted service is required to run sandboxes. Source builds fetch Bazel dependencies over the network (MODULE.bazel:38-121).

languages: Go (primary: pkg/, runsc/, shim/, webhook/, sandboxexec/sandbox, tools/; ~845 Go files under pkg/sentry alone)
Go assembly (amd64/arm64 .s files under pkg/, e.g. pkg/safecopy, pkg/ring0, pkg/sentry/platform/systrap)
C++ (syscall/perf/packetimpact tests under test/; vDSO in vdso/)

entry_points.what: `runsc` binary: OCI runtime and user CLI; delegates to runsc/cli/maincli (subcommand registry at maincli.go:49-103).
`gvisor_sentry` sidecar binary that runs the Sentry (the gVisor kernel); internal boot/umount/symbolize commands.
`runsc bwrap` bubblewrap-style CLI personality (also reached when the binary is named `bwrap`, runsc/cmd/alias/aliases.go:35-44); translation in bwrap.go.
`runsc sandboxexec`: starts a sandbox from a SandboxOptions proto (sandboxexec/proto/sandbox_options.proto) and prints PID and control-socket path (lines 185-187).
`runsc do`: quick one-off command in a sandbox with host fs read-only plus in-memory overlay; documented as testing-only.
Experimental Go SDK; Python counterpart at sandboxexec/sandbox/python/gvisor/sandbox.py (package `gvisor`).
Checkpoint-gofer sidecar for remote (GCS) checkpoint file access; other sidecars listed in tools/release.bzl:35-40.

code.architecture: Per sandbox, `runsc` (runsc/main.go -> runsc/cli/maincli; OCI/CLI commands in runsc/cmd; sandbox/gofer process management in runsc/sandbox and runsc/container; flags/config in runsc/config; OCI spec handling in runsc/specutils) starts (1) the Sentry userspace kernel as the `gvisor_sentry` sidecar (runsc/cmd/sentry, boot logic runsc/boot): Linux syscall tables in pkg/sentry/syscalls/linux/linux64.go, task/process model in pkg/sentry/kernel, VFS in pkg/sentry/vfs with filesystems in pkg/sentry/fsimpl, memory in pkg/sentry/mm, sockets in pkg/sentry/socket on the netstack TCP/IP stack in pkg/tcpip (or host sockets with --network=host), Linux ABI definitions in pkg/abi/linux, syscall/fault-interception platforms in pkg/sentry/platform/{systrap (default),kvm,ptrace}, GPU/TPU/RDMA proxies in pkg/sentry/devices/{nvproxy,tpuproxy,rdmaproxy}, audit/trace in pkg/sentry/seccheck; the Sentry's own host-syscall allowlist is built in runsc/boot/filter/config on pkg/seccomp ('all syscalls the sandbox is allowed to make to the host', config.go:15-16, with HostNetwork/HostFilesystem options at :36-50); and (2) the Gofer (runsc/fsgofer, LISAFS protocol in pkg/lisafs) that owns filesystem access, with 'directfs' letting the Sentry operate on donated FDs (g3doc/user_guide/filesystem.md:72-94). Sidecars in gvisor-bin/: checkpointgofer, runsc-metric-server, runsc-fd-parking, gvisor-sentry-prewarmer (tools/release.bzl:21-40). Integration code: containerd shim (shim/), mutating Kubernetes webhook (webhook/), SandboxExec SDKs+proto (sandboxexec/), CLI personalities (runsc/cmd/alias/bwrap, runsc/cmd/sandboxexec.go, runsc/cmd/do.go). Build: Bazel (MODULE.bazel; .bazelversion = 8.3.1) wrapped by the Makefile; tools/ holds build/analysis tooling (nogo, checklocks, checkescape, checkunsafe...); docs in g3doc/ and website/.
code.packaging_and_release: Releases are built by an internal Buildkite pipeline, not GitHub Actions: .buildkite/release.yaml:49-63 stages the tag, builds x86_64 and aarch64 artifacts in opt mode, builds Python wheels, runs `make release`, copies to gs://gvisor/releases/ and then pushes the release tag (.buildkite/scripts/release/tag.sh:17-23). Artifacts per arch: gvisor.tar.bz2 and gvisor.tar.zstd (runsc + containerd-shim-runsc-v1 + gvisor-bin/ sidecars; debian/BUILD:80-120), a `runsc` .deb (debian/BUILD:53-78), and a Python wheel/sdist (tools/make_python_release.sh:96-134). Integrity: a .sha512 file is generated beside each raw artifact (tools/make_release.sh:51-80); the apt repo is GPG-signed with InRelease/Release.gpg using SHA512 digests (tools/make_apt.sh:164-168) and .debs are signed with dpkg-sig (make_apt.sh:121-122); the public key is served from https://gvisor.dev/archive.key (install.md:27). GitHub Releases are a mirror: .github/workflows/release_mirror.yml triggers on tags matching release-YYYYMMDD.N (lines 14-23,50), waits for the GCS artifacts, verifies sha512, renames per architecture, generates SHA256SUMS and SHA512SUMS, and attaches them (lines 113-143,181-215); the workflow states it builds nothing (lines 3-8). No cosign/Sigstore/SLSA/provenance/attestation tooling was found in .github, .buildkite or tools. Python: wheels are staged to Google's 'OSS Exit Gate' Artifact Registry (tools/make_python_release.sh:168-210); docs say `pip install gvisor` and tools/make_release.sh:127-129 says PyPI is canonical, but PyPI publication cannot be verified from this tree. Version scheme is date-based release-YYYYMMDD.N, with nightly and master channels (install.md:120-156,173-207).
code.tests_and_ci: Frameworks: Go `testing` under Bazel go_test; C++ gtest syscall tests run both natively and under runsc via the `syscall_test()` macro (test/syscalls/BUILD; .claude/skills/add-syscall/SKILL.md:156-161); Python unittest for the SDK; packetdrill/packetimpact network tests; Docker/containerd/Podman/Kubernetes e2e; Go/Java/Node/PHP/Python language-runtime suites; a syzkaller smoke test; benchmarks. Approximate test-file counts (from globs): ~570 Go *_test.go (pkg 344, runsc 62, test 139, sandboxexec+shim+tools 23), ~296 C++ .cc files in test/syscalls/linux (432 .cc/.h under test/), 2 Python test files (sandboxexec/sandbox/python/tests/sandbox_test.py, g3doc/user_guide/sdk/python_docs_api_test.py). CI: primary pipeline is Buildkite (.buildkite/pipeline.yaml): smoke and race tests, builds, nogo static analysis, unit/container tests on cgroup v1/v2 and ARM64, syscall tests on KVM/systrap including release-candidate Linux kernels, Docker/containerd 1.7-2.2/Podman/Kubernetes integration, GPU/CUDA tests, bwrap tests (lines 758-774), 'sandbox posture' tests that compare the host-observable security posture of the Sentry process against the configured expectations (lines 569-577; pkg/test/sandboxposture/sandboxposture.go:15-18), lint, dependency license check (lines 336-341), governance check (lines 330-335), and benchmark jobs (lines 29-48,836-917); .buildkite/release.yaml adds release and GPU jobs; .buildkite/pgo.yaml refreshes PGO profiles. GitHub Actions: build.yml (builds runsc), go.yml (generates/pushes the `go` branch and runs `go build ./...`), lint.yml (`make lint`), fileheader.yml (license headers), codeql.yml (daily; go, javascript, python, ruby), release_mirror.yml, issue_reviver.yml, labeler.yml, stale.yml, auto_assign.yml, close_banned_prs.yml; dependabot updates GitHub Actions weekly (.github/dependabot.yml:6-14). macOS/Windows/FreeBSD/OpenBSD/32-bit steps only cross-build selected netstack packages (.buildkite/pipeline.yaml:146-196).
code.dependencies: go.mod (go 1.26.3, line 3): 43 direct requires (go.mod:5-49) and 80 indirect (go.mod:51-132). MODULE.bazel: 18 bazel_dep modules (MODULE.bazel:6-23) plus archive overrides for rules_go/grpc and http_archive pins for llvm and kythe (MODULE.bazel:25-70), with Go modules pulled from go.mod through gazelle; Bazel version in .bazelversion:1 (8.3.1). Python SDK: 0 runtime dependencies (sandboxexec/sandbox/python/pyproject.toml:26). Dependency licenses are recorded in tools/licensecheck/dependencies.yaml. `make license-check` (Makefile:214-216; .buildkite/pipeline.yaml:336-341) verifies that every dependency has an entry there, and TestLicensePolicy (tools/licensecheck/licensecheck_test.go:185-201) checks each entry against the allowed list in governance/licensing.yaml:10-29 (Apache-2.0, 0BSD, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-2-Clause-FreeBSD, BSD-3-Clause, MIT, MIT-0, ISC, OpenSSL, OpenSSL-standalone, PSF-2.0, Python-2.0, Python-2.0.1, PostgreSQL, SSLeay-standalone, UPL-1.0, X11, Zlib, 'Google patent license for Golang'). Three entries are listed exceptions (governance/licensing.yaml:30-55): google_root_pem (NOASSERTION; CA root bundle for test images only, never in released binaries; dependencies.yaml:911-916), grpc (Apache-2.0, BSD-3-Clause, MPL-2.0; Bazel build/test tooling only, released binaries use pure-Go google.golang.org/grpc; dependencies.yaml:949-957) and llvm-raw (Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception, MIT; NVIDIA GPU test toolchain only, not distributed; dependencies.yaml:1008-1015). MPL-2.0 (file-level copyleft) is the only copyleft-family identifier in dependencies.yaml and appears only on that Bazel-side grpc archive; no GPL/LGPL/AGPL identifiers appear in the file. Core Sentry packages avoid external imports by policy (g3doc/architecture_guide/security.md:206-209). The project's own source is not uniformly Apache-2.0 (see the license field and the licensing risk).
code.security_policy: SECURITY.md (repo root): private reports to gvisor-security@googlegroups.com or GitHub security advisories, typical response within 48h (SECURITY.md:3-7); CVEs only for gVisor-specific issues that cross the sandbox boundary where the attacker does not control the sandbox configuration (SECURITY.md:9-17); operator-controlled config (OCI spec, runtime flags such as --network=host) is out of CVE scope (SECURITY.md:144-176,254-261); disclosure/embargo process is in GOVERNANCE.md (SECURITY.md:272-275). The experimental sandboxexec directory is declared 'not yet a valid target for security issues' (sandboxexec/README.md:6-18).

claim_checks.claim: README.md:11-14,23-26 - application kernel in memory-safe Go; 'not a syscall filter' nor 'a wrapper over Linux isolation primitives'.
claim_checks.evidence: Consistent on the core point: syscalls are implemented by the Sentry rather than passed through (pkg/sentry/syscalls/linux/linux64.go:15 'syscall tables for amd64 and arm64 Linux'; g3doc/architecture_guide/intro_to_gvisor.md:100-105). But gVisor also layers host seccomp, namespaces and pivot_root under the Sentry as a second layer (runsc/boot/filter/config/config.go:15-16; SECURITY.md:64-67; intro_to_gvisor.md:124-133). 'Memory-safe Go' is qualified: unsafe code is confined to *_unsafe.go files by policy (g3doc/architecture_guide/security.md:202-204), the tree contains Go assembly (e.g. pkg/safecopy/memcpy_amd64.s, pkg/sentry/platform/systrap/stub_amd64.s), a C++ vDSO (vdso/vdso.cc), and optional cgo only in the network-plugin build (pkg/sentry/socket/plugin/cgo/stack_unsafe.go; .bazelrc:33-37 selects pure Go by default).

claim_checks.claim: README.md:48-51 - gVisor is not a tool to 'limit the scope of access for a service'; be careful what data is made available.
claim_checks.evidence: Access scope is whatever the OCI spec/mounts and --network mode supply: three network modes (runsc/config/config.go:743-758; flags.go:160) and bind/tmpfs/overlay mounts (g3doc/user_guide/filesystem.md:12-54). No per-path/glob or per-domain policy engine exists in code: sandboxexec/proto/sandbox_options.proto:34-39 declares domain_allowlist/domain_denylist but a repo-wide search finds no other reference. g3doc/architecture_guide/security.md:172-177 says network policy controls should be applied at the container level; SECURITY.md:189-198 treats operator-configured host mounts as intended exposure.

Documented in two places, but no code gate on 5.6 found. Kernel-version comparisons in non-test code exist only for KVM on arm64 (pkg/sentry/platform/kvm/kvm_arm64_unsafe.go:63); other gating is feature-specific: cgroup v2/clone3 probing (runsc/cgroup/cgroup_v2_unsafe.go:45-56), core tagging needs >=5.14 (runsc/config/flags.go:117), systrap note 'available since Linux 5.0' (pkg/sentry/platform/systrap/subprocess.go:201). README lists 5.6 under 'Installing from source > Requirements' while install.md presents it as a general requirement. Startup host-setting checks (user namespaces) are in runsc/hostsettings/hostsettings.go:254-312.

claim_checks.claim: README.md:76-83 - release tarball contains runsc, containerd-shim-runsc-v1 and sidecars in gvisor-bin/; built with `make release-tarball DESTINATION=bin/`.
claim_checks.evidence: Makefile:915-919 builds //debian:gvisor-release-tar-bz2 and -zstd; debian/BUILD:80-120 bundles //runsc, //shim:containerd-shim-runsc-v1 and gvisor-bin-tar; sidecars are gvisor_sentry, checkpointgofer, runsc-metric-server, runsc-fd-parking and gvisor-sentry-prewarmer (tools/release.bzl:21-40).

claim_checks.claim: g3doc/user_guide/install.md:84-101 - `runsc install` sidecar auto-download is dropped at the end of September 2026.
claim_checks.evidence: Still present at release-20260928.0: --download-sidecars defaults to IF_RELEASE_BUILD with help text 'will go away in a few weeks' (runsc/cmd/install.go:69-73) and the downloader shells out to curl/wget against storage.googleapis.com (runsc/cmd/install_sidecars.go:46-70). The embedded-binary fallback is already off by default (runsc/config/config.go:1496-1503) though its flag help says it 'will stop working after 2026-10' (runsc/config/flags.go:122) and maincli still imports the embed package (runsc/cli/maincli/maincli.go:29-31). Code is ahead of/behind the doc depending on the flag.

claim_checks.claim: g3doc/user_guide/sdk/go.md:45-49,124-132 and quickstart.md:14-15,36-50 - Go SDK offers `WithNetworking(bool)` and `Exec(ctx, cmd, opts ...string) (stdout, stderr string, err error)`; Go 1.16+ suffices.
claim_checks.evidence: Code wins and differs: the option is `WithNetwork(mode NetworkMode)` (sandboxexec/sandbox/sandbox.go:161) and `Exec(ctx, argv []string, opts ...ExecOption) (*ExecResult, error)` (sandbox.go:687); `WithNetworking` appears only in the two doc files (repo-wide search). The code uses `slices` (sandboxexec/sandbox/oci.go:22) and `errors.Join` (sandbox.go:775), which need far newer Go than 1.16 (go.mod:3 declares 1.26.3). Python docs, by contrast, are checked against code for symbol coverage (g3doc/user_guide/sdk/python_docs_api_test.py:15), though python_quickstart.md:14 says Python 3.9+ while pyproject.toml:10 declares >=3.7.

claim_checks.claim: g3doc/user_guide/sdk/python.md:55-56 and examples/sandboxexec/python/README.md:43-45 - SDK network defaults to `none`; `Mount.bind(..., readonly=True)` is read-only.
claim_checks.evidence: Python default NetworkMode.NONE (sandboxexec/sandbox/python/gvisor/sandbox.py:293) is passed as `--network=none` (sandbox.py:389); Go default is NetworkModeNone (sandboxexec/sandbox/sandbox.go:359-363,413-417); read-only mounts map to the OCI `ro` option (sandbox.py:496-504; oci.go:125-127) and a test asserts a write to a read-only bind mount fails (sandboxexec/sandbox/python/tests/sandbox_test.py:438-458). Caveats: runsc's own default is `--network=sandbox` (runsc/config/flags.go:160); `runsc sandboxexec` leaves that default unless the proto sets networking_options (runsc/cmd/sandboxexec.go:278-285); the SDK test for `none` only asserts the OCI spec lacks a network namespace entry (sandbox_test.py:400-410), not that connections fail; the root fs is an empty bundle dir (oci.go:146-150; sandbox.py:461-466), read-only in Python (sandbox.py:533-537) but writable by default in Go (oci.go:177-180); host /bin,/usr,/lib,/lib64,/etc/alternatives are bound read-only by default (oci.go:34,222-237; sandbox.py:484-494).

claim_checks.claim: g3doc/user_guide/personalities/bwrap.md:45,92,101-103 and 61-63 - `--unshare-net` -> `--network=none`; without it `--network=host`; `--ro-bind` is read-only; without a root mount a fresh tmpfs root is used.

risks: Platform: Linux-only. FAQ says 'Today, gVisor requires Linux' (g3doc/user_guide/FAQ.md:5-7); macOS is documented only for running some Bazel test targets (README.md:125-135) and CI only cross-builds netstack packages for darwin/arm64 (.buildkite/pipeline.yaml:146-156); the project's Dangerzone post says gVisor 'works strictly on Linux systems' and that macOS/Windows use needs a Linux VM (website/blog/2024-09-23-dangerzone.md:83-85,305-314). WSL2 is not mentioned anywhere in the tree (all file types searched) and has no CI job, so support there is undocumented/unknown; startup checks user-namespace sysctls and rootless mode needs unprivileged user namespaces (runsc/hostsettings/hostsettings.go:254-312).

Network deny-by-default is opt-in per entry point, not a runtime default: runsc's own `--network` default is `sandbox` (runsc/config/flags.go:160) and `runsc do` builds a veth+iptables NAT path to the host unless `--network=none` (runsc/cmd/do.go:252-273,309-344); only `none` yields loopback-only networking (runsc/sandbox/network.go:58-63). The SDKs default to none (sandboxexec/sandbox/sandbox.go:359-363; sandboxexec/sandbox/python/gvisor/sandbox.py:293), but `runsc bwrap` defaults to host networking unless `--unshare-net` (runsc/cmd/alias/bwrap/bwrap.go:254-257), has an open TODO on network args (bwrap.go:267) and rejects `--share-net` (cli.go:436-439), and `runsc sandboxexec` only selects `none` when the proto contains networking_options (runsc/cmd/sandboxexec.go:278-285). No per-domain allow/deny list is implemented although declared in sandboxexec/proto/sandbox_options.proto:34-39 (no other reference in the repo). Sandbox-network mode needs root (sandboxexec/sandbox/sandbox.go:502-504; g3doc/architecture_guide/intro_to_gvisor.md:219-226); rootless supports only none/host networking and no save/restore (g3doc/user_guide/rootless.md:46-53). I found no SDK or bwrap test asserting that outbound connections actually fail under `none`.

Maturity of the agent-facing surfaces: the SandboxExec Go/Python SDKs and `runsc sandboxexec` are labelled experimental and 'not meant for production use' (sandboxexec/README.md:3-4; g3doc/user_guide/sdk/go.md:3-4), at version 0.1.0 (sandboxexec/sandbox/python/pyproject.toml:7), and the directory is declared not a valid target for security reports, including a line addressed to AI agents/automated scanners (sandboxexec/README.md:6-18). Go SDK docs do not match the code (see claim_checks); sandboxexec/proto/defaults.textproto uses `sandbox_path` keys that the proto does not define (defaults.textproto:75-80 vs sandbox_options.proto:78-84) and nothing references it; the project blog calls integration into existing applications a 'current drawback' that 'is being worked on' (website/blog/2026-04-15-magi-multi-agent-gvisor-isolation.md:1318-1321). No MCP server and no Claude Code/Codex integration exist.

Scope and filesystem exposure are operator-defined: README says gVisor is not a tool to 'limit the scope of access for a service' (README.md:48-51); the security policy treats operator-configured host mounts as intended behaviour (SECURITY.md:189-198) and assigns CVEs only to gVisor-specific sandbox-boundary escapes where the attacker does not control the sandbox configuration, so misconfiguration or runtime flags such as `--network=host` are out of CVE scope (SECURITY.md:9-17,254-261); the production guide lists running untrusted code as a use case but says the guide itself 'is not appropriate for this use-case' and focuses on running an existing trusted stack (g3doc/user_guide/production.md:25-28). `runsc do` is 'for testing only' and exposes host `/` read-only through an in-memory overlay; `--force-overlay=false` gives write access to the host (runsc/cmd/do.go:69-81,148,153). SDK sandboxes bind host /bin, /usr, /lib, /lib64, /etc/alternatives read-only by default (sandboxexec/sandbox/oci.go:34,222-237; sandbox.py:484-494), and the bwrap personality inherits the full host environment (runsc/cmd/alias/bwrap/cli.go:152-155; g3doc/user_guide/personalities/bwrap.md:172-173).

Install/layout is mid-transition: `runsc` needs sidecars in `gvisor-bin/` next to it, so copying a bare binary is insufficient (g3doc/user_guide/install.md:59-63,78-82); the default sidecar policy disallows the embedded fallback (runsc/config/config.go:1496-1503), whose flag help says it 'will stop working after 2026-10' (runsc/config/flags.go:122); `runsc install` auto-download (needs network plus curl/wget) is slated for removal at end of Sept 2026 but is still present at this tag (install.md:84-101; runsc/cmd/install.go:69-73); `runsc install` rewrites Docker daemon config, /etc/docker/daemon.json by default (runsc/cmd/install.go:53-55,64).

Release integrity: GitHub release assets are a mirror of artifacts built by an internal Buildkite pipeline (.github/workflows/release_mirror.yml:3-8; .buildkite/release.yaml:49-63); checksums are sha512 sidecars plus SHA256SUMS/SHA512SUMS generated by the mirror workflow itself (release_mirror.yml:113-143); only the apt repository and .debs are GPG/dpkg-sig signed (tools/make_apt.sh:121-122,164-168); no Sigstore/cosign/SLSA/attestation tooling found in .github, .buildkite or tools. Python wheels are staged to Google's Artifact Registry (tools/make_python_release.sh:168-210); PyPI publication cannot be verified from this repo.

Compatibility and overhead: gVisor implements a subset of Linux - iptables only partially, block-device filesystems (ext4/fat32) not mountable in-sandbox, io_uring off by default, in-sandbox cgroup limits not enforced (g3doc/user_guide/compatibility.md:45-70). Syscall-, network- and file-I/O-heavy workloads degrade (g3doc/user_guide/production.md:74-80); the project's own microbenchmarks (undated, ptrace platform, Debian 9 VMs) show 38,219 ns per syscall vs 1,939 ns native (website/performance/syscall.csv:2-3; g3doc/architecture_guide/performance.md:44-64). The ptrace platform is documented as no longer supported (g3doc/user_guide/platforms.md:48-54).

Governance and licensing: all 17 listed active maintainers list Google as their organization, with 13 emeritus entries (MAINTAINERS.md:8-24,36-50); contributions require a Google CLA (CONTRIBUTING.md:5-15). The source is not Apache-2.0 alone: the root LICENSE holds Apache-2.0 (LICENSE:1-202), then an MIT notice (LICENSE:204-224) and a BSD-3-Clause notice (LICENSE:226-254) for files that carry those licenses 'noted at the top of each file'; the README has no license statement. BSD-style headers are on 30 source files: 23 under pkg/sync and 2 under pkg/hostarch (gVisor-authored, e.g. pkg/sync/sync.go:1-5, pkg/hostarch/hostarch.go:1-5), four Go-derived pkg/safecopy assembly files (memcpy_arm64.s, memclr_arm64.s, memclr_amd64.s, atomic_arm64.s) and pkg/sentry/time/arith_arm64.go:1-10, with per-directory Go-Authors BSD LICENSE files in pkg/sync, pkg/safecopy and pkg/sentry/time. The MIT notice (Lucent Technologies / Vita Nuova / Go Authors) is on pkg/safecopy/memcpy_amd64.s:1-21. These packages are linked into the Sentry (pkg/sentry/mm/pma.go imports pkg/safecopy; pkg/sentry/kernel/kernel.go:80 imports pkg/sentry/time; runsc/cli/cli.go:35 imports pkg/sync; runsc/cmd/sentry/sentrycmd/boot.go imports pkg/hostarch); the BSD text requires binary redistributions to reproduce its copyright notice and disclaimer (LICENSE:236-238) and the MIT text requires its notice in all copies or substantial portions (LICENSE:215-216). The gVisor logo files are CC BY-SA 4.0 (g3doc/logo.txt:1); the Python SDK package declares Apache-2.0 (sandboxexec/sandbox/python/pyproject.toml:11). Third-party dependency licenses are summarised under code.dependencies (includes an MPL-2.0 entry limited to Bazel build/test tooling, governance/licensing.yaml:37-46).

checks.note: LICENSE opens with the full Apache License 2.0 (1-202), so Apache-2.0 is the primary license. But the same file goes on to say that 'Some files carry the following license' for MIT (204-224) and for the 'BSD' license, which is the Go-style BSD-3-Clause text (226-254). Those files are compiled into runsc. The gVisor-authored core packages pkg/sync (sync.go:1-5) and pkg/hostarch (hostarch.go:1-5) use the BSD-style header pointing to LICENSE. So do the Go-derived pkg/safecopy/*.s files and pkg/sentry/time/arith_arm64.go, and pkg/sync, pkg/safecopy and pkg/sentry/time each have their own BSD LICENSE file. pkg/safecopy/memcpy_amd64.s:1-21 is MIT (Lucent/Vita Nuova/Go). The single identifier 'Apache-2.0' therefore leaves out two licenses that the cited file itself declares. All three are permissive and there is no copyleft, so this is a completeness and attribution error, not a wrong license family.
